name: 0046 block 3d - VFD driven 600 rpm, sinus OFF, 10 min
description: BLOCK 3d — VFD DRIVEN FROM THE PI, sinus output filter OFF. Replaces the hand-driven variant at Kim's suggestion (2026-10-01), and the reason is that it turns 'slowly' into a NUMBER: the commanded speed goes into the telemetry and is stamped onto EVERY SWEEP (telem_rpm_target / telem_vfd_cmd_hz), so blocks 3d and 4d are measured at exactly the same speed instead of 'slowly' twice. The sinus-filter delta is the whole point of this pair, so that matters. SCHEDULE: 1 min at rest, 8 min at 600 rpm, 1 min at rest. 600 rpm = 10.084 Hz, which is the best-characterised point on this rig (measured 591 rpm against the calibration's 591.6, 0.6 %). The rest minutes at either end give an in-block floor, so drive EMI can be read as a step rather than only as a delta against another run. BASELINE: block 2B. Heater/temp control box stays OFF (2B left it off; block 4b switches it back on later as its own test). Everything else as block 2B: 24 V sensor supply linear, slip-ring/OE linear, heater relay open, external tachometer off. CAVEAT TO KNOW, NOT TO FEAR: driving the VFD adds Modbus WRITES on the shared RS485 bus on top of the status reads the runner already does every tick. That is traffic during a noise measurement. It is small — the bus is active in every block including the floor, where the writes merely failed against a dead drive — and it is IDENTICAL in 3d and 4d, so it cancels in the sinus delta. Do not compare these two blocks' absolute floors against block 0 without remembering it. max_consecutive_modbus_errors is left at its normal default: the drive is energized and answering, so the runner's safety stop is doing its proper job and must not be raised.
